text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Speaking at the Parliamentary Assebmbly of the Council of Europe, President Guntis Ulmanis announced a moratorium on capital punishment in Latvia.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele addressed the U.N. General Assembly and signed the nuclear test ban treaty, although Latvia has no nuclear capability.

- Shkele failed to meet U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot and arrived late for a reception organised by State Secretary Warren Christopher because of technical problems with the aircraft carrying the Latvian delegation.
- Police believe that the assassination of leading businessman Valery Machugin was ordered by his business rivals.

- The cabinet decided to stop using work record cards for calculating a person's length of service after January 1, 1997, when the new labour code takes effect. The main document for counting the amount of pension will be the person's contract with the employer the and tax record book.
- Juris Celminsh, the deputy head of the Democratic Party Saimnieks who was accused of having been an agent of the KGB, has decided to go to the Prosecutor's office before being officially summoned.

- Riga City Council decided to put off the start of the heating season because of consumers debts amounting to 26.4 million lats. According to regulations, the heating should be switched on when the average daily temperature falls below eight degrees centigrade for four consecutive days.
- The Ministry of Transport has formed a working group to work on organising a ferry line between Latvia and Sweden.
- A German transport and dispatching company, Kuhne & Naegel, opened a new cargo terminal and warehouse in Riga.
